title: प्रथमोनुवाकः
samhita: शि॒वेन॒ वच॑सा त्वा॒ गिरि॒शाच्छा॑ वदामसि । यथा॑ न॒-स्सर्व॒मिज्जग॑दय॒क्ष्मग्ं सु॒मना॒ अस॑त् ॥
pada: शि॒वेन॑ । वच॑सा । त्वा॒ । गिरि॑श । अच्छ॑ । व॒दा॒म॒सि॒  ॥ यथा᳚ । नः॒ । सर्व᳚म । इत । जग॑त । अ॒य॒क्ष्मम । सु॒मना॒ इति॑ सु = मना᳚: । अस॑त ॥

sayana.text:
Sayana's Commentary: O Girisha, you who reside (shete) on the mountain (giri) Kailasa—we pray to you (tvaam) with auspicious (shiva), welfare-causing words in the form of praise. So that (yatha) our entire moving world (nah sarvam-it jagat)—the word 'it' is for emphasis—all beings including humans and animals, may be free from disease (ayakshmam) and endowed with a good mind (sumana). Do thus. (5)

Bhatta-Bhaskara-Bhashya: Now the second (of this pair). 'Shivenavachasa'. O Girisha—he who resides (shete) on the mountain (giri) Kailasa. Or, he who has the mountain as his excellent residence. Or, he who is the Lord (Isha) of the mountain (Kailasa), or the cloud (giri), or of speech (giraam) in the form of the Veda and Pranava. With auspicious speech (shivena vachasa)—with words of the nature of a hymn of praise, which consists of the recitation of your qualities, or which is welfare-causing, or which is pleasing to you—we speak (vadamasi) toward you (tvaam) who are endowed with all lordly qualities. We praise you—this is the meaning. 'Vadamasi' is the Vedic form for 'vadamah'. In the text, the word 'achha' has a long 'a' due to Vedic rules. The indeclinable 'achha' means 'toward'. Some say it is in the sense of 'to attain'.

Indeed, with non-auspicious speech, the God might become angry. As it is said: "Let us not provoke you, O Rudra, let us not (offend you) with our salutations, O Bull, nor with ill-timed cries or joined invocations." Therefore, we praise you with auspicious words. If it is asked why, he says: so that (yatha) our entire moving world (sarvam-it jagat)—all beings, progeny, cattle, etc. The word 'it' includes stationary things like trees as well. 'Ayakshmam'—free from disease. 'Sumana'—here the gender changes; it means endowed with a good mind (soumanasya). 'Asat'—may it be so. It is the fifth mood (Let). This is the kind of thing for which we praise you. Or, in response to the question 'how?', he says: we praise you in such a way that while you are being praised, this (welfare) comes to pass.

For these two (mantras 4 and 5), the Purashcharana is continuous chanting for twenty-one days. Then, having completed the Purashcharana, one should perform the prevention of untimely death (akaala-marana) with these. A king should have it performed by a perfected Brahmin; then untimely death does not occur in the kingdom. With these two, one should offer a lakh (100,000) of oblations of sesame, rice, cow-ghee, and barley, smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, over twenty-one days. In that kingdom, there is no fear of untimely death. In nine days, disturbances vanish. In eighteen days, untimely death is pacified in the whole world.

Meditation (Dhyanam):
"One should meditate on the Enemy of the Cities (Purari), shining with a body prepared for battle, with a gentle smile that is like a thunderbolt to the straw-like three cities, desiring to burn the demons, holding the Mountain-Lord (Meru) as a bow in his hand, and mounted on a chariot consisting of the assembly of gods." (5)

bhatta_bhaskara.dhyana: Meditation on Shiva as detailed in standard commentaries.

abhinava_shankara.dhyana: Meditation on Lord Maheshvara with resplendent Goddess.
abhinava_shankara.text:
SRI RUDRA BHASHYAM.                       53

Having thus bowed down saying 'namaste rudra', and having prayed for the warding off of undesirable harms through the second, third, and fourth mantras addressed to Girisha; now, [the devotee] prays with praise for the removal of fear regarding the physical body — stated in 'Shivenavachasa'.

By the word 'giri', the Vedas which are in the form of mountains are meant; as the Shruti states: 'He showed them as three unknown mountain-like forms', introducing 'these are indeed the Vedas'. Thus, He who resides (shete) or stays in the Vedas that are like mountains is 'Girisha' — the one revealed by the Vedas.

O Girisha! 'Achha' means clearly and purely. We speak to You ('tvam shivena vachasa vadamasi') — meaning we praise You with auspicious words.

What kind of praise is it? He answers: 'Yatha' — in such a manner that through this praise, 'nah' — pertaining to us, 'sarvam it' — absolutely all, 'jagat' — the moving creation comprising children, cattle, etc., 'ayakshmam' — free from disease, and 'sumanah' — endowed with happiness and composure of mind, 'asat' — may become so; in that manner we praise You.

Here, by using the word 'Girisha', it is shown that it is most appropriate to offer praise to Him who is celebrated in all the Vedas.
